title: git show
definition: Shows one or more objects (blobs, trees, tags and commits). Most commonly used to see the exact code changes introduced by a specific commit.
simpleExplanation: `git log` tells you THAT a commit happened. `git show` tells you exactly WHAT code was added or deleted inside that commit.
realWorldExample: You see a commit titled 'Fix header'. You type `git show <hash>` to see exactly which CSS lines were changed to fix the header.

basic: If you just type `git show` without a hash, what does it show?
intermediate: In the output of `git show`, what do lines starting with `+` and `-` mean?

answers.question: Without a hash?
answers.answer: It defaults to showing the very latest commit on your current branch (also known as `HEAD`).

answers.question: + and - lines?
answers.answer: `+` (usually in green) indicates a line of code that was added. `-` (usually in red) indicates a line of code that was deleted.

tableData.title: `git show` Flags
rows: Shows the log message and textual diff of the specific commit.
Shows only the list of modified files and how many lines were added/removed.
Shows only the raw file names that were changed.
Shows the very last commit you made.
